title: Hybrid decoder scenarios for streaming JSON-mode validation and schema fallback
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create an end-to-end test harness and validation logic for a hybrid decoding path that mixes constrained deterministic decoding with stochastic sampling during streaming JSON mode. This ticket builds a scenario suite that exercises partial-stream reassembly, mid-stream tool/function call insertion, and a schema-aware validator that can trigger graceful fallback or on-the-fly repair (e.g., close unclosed arrays/objects, insert sentinel tokens, or request a refactor completion from the model). The goal is to detect and codify failure modes that lead to schema violation in production streaming responses and to validate automatic remediation strategies.
acceptance_criteria: A set of at least 12 distinct scenario manifests covering truncation, token drift, interleaved tool-call payloads, KV-cache-induced repetition, and high-entropy sampling during tail tokens
Automated harness that runs these scenarios against constrained-decoder, hybrid-decoder, and unconstrained baseline and records schema pass/fail and correction actions
A prototype schema-aware runtime hook that can repair two common class of violations (missing closing bracket, malformed field value) and empirically reduces failures by >= 70% on CI smoke runs
PR with unit and integration tests merged and a follow-up rollout plan in runtime-1.21 release notes
test_plan: Generate synthetic prompts that exercise nested JSON shapes and variable-length arrays with streaming lengths
Inject simulated network truncation at multiple byte offsets and assert validator recovers or signals retry
Interleave tool call responses mid-stream and assert that the schema validator tolerates partial tool payloads until tool-call closure
Measure detection latency (ms) from first invalid token to remediation action across decoders
Run scenarios on target GPU profiles (A10G, H100-like) to ensure kernel scheduling doesn't change tokenization or emission ordering assumptions
implementation_steps: Design scenario manifest format and serializer (jsonlines, one scenario per file)
Implement streaming schema validator shim that consumes token deltas and emits structured-delta diagnostics
Wire validator into hybrid decoding path as a non-blocking hook with configurable policy (repair, signal-retry, mark-bad)
Add CI jobs that run the harness against three decoder modes and surface a summary artifact to testgrid
Iterate on remediation heuristics with Product/RE to avoid unsafe repairs that mask model defects
notes: 2025-11-04: Spike completed showing repair heuristics (close-bracket, numeric-cast-fallback) work on simple streams; larger nested schemas still fail in ~18% of cases
2025-11-06: Discussed with PM about UX when runtime repairs output (should we annotate responses or return a 206-like partial+repair header?) — leaning toward annotation until product decision
Trade-offs: aggressive auto-repair reduces visible errors but can hide model drift; conservative policy requires more retries and hurts latency. We will parameterize this behavior per customer tier.
Performance: validator must operate in O(delta) per token; initial implementation uses a lightweight stack and heuristics to avoid full-parse on every token
review_feedback: PM (Sara Liu): annotate repaired responses and expose repair_reason in Console for transparency
Design (Kavita Singh): include example UX for partial/annotated streaming responses in console and API docs
Security (Tom Becker): ensure repairs do not insert sensitive placeholders; validator must not synthesize PII

risks: Auto-repair may change semantics of responses and break downstream parsers if not annotated
Repair heuristics might become a crutch hiding regressions in model sampling or tokenization
Edge cases with tool/function calls can produce ambiguous boundaries; worst-case leads to silent data loss if not surfaced
Too heavy validation per-token can increase tail latency and violate SLOs for P0 customers
observability_checks: Expose metric: streaming_schema_failure_count by scenario, decoder-mode, model-version
Add tracing span that marks when repair was attempted and which heuristic succeeded
Create dashboard card showing mean time-to-detect and mean time-to-repair for hybrid-decoder runs
next_steps: Finish CI stabilization and reduce flakes in GPU-backed runs
Deliver a short RFC describing annotation + repair policies for product review
Run a canary on dedicated cluster for one low-risk customer with monitoring and opt-out flag
